headline: Reviewed draft Comprehensive Plan and Future Land Use map; approved the previous meeting minutes.
summary: The meeting covered the draft Comprehensive Plan, including its overview, the Future Land Use map, and draft land use goals. It also reviewed zoning incentives for priority and inclusionary housing projects. The only recorded vote was to approve the previous meeting minutes, which passed unanimously.
decisions: Approved the previous meeting minutes unanimously; motion carried.

9/10/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Members Present: Mike O’Brien, Chair; Trevor Thomas; Brian Colombini; James Paradissis; 
John Baker
City Staff Present: Ravi Venkataraman, Director of City Planning
Guests Present: Eli Ogilvie, Bryn Oakleaf, Thomas Renner
Call to Order by: Mike
Meeting Start Time: 6:30 pm
Minutes Recorded by: Ravi
Changes to the Agenda
None
Public Comment
None
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
Motion by: Trevor
Second: Brian
Decision: Unanimous. Motion Carried.
Discussion: Winooski Comprehensive Plan – General Overview; the approach for the 
update; the Future Land Use map; and the draft Land Use goals and actions
Ravi gave a general overview of the Comprehensive Plan. Ravi and Mike discussed the 
relationship between the Comprehensive Plan and the zoning regulations. Ravi and Mike 
discussed the required housing elements for the Comprehensive Plan and the regional housing 
targets. Ravi reviewed the public engagement the City has done in general and for the 
Comprehensive Plan.
Ravi noted the role of the Equitable Housing Needs Assessment in the Comprehensive Plan. 
Brian asked if a presentation on the Equitable Housing Needs Assessment will be provided. Ravi 
said that that can be penciled in after the project is completed at the end of the year.
Ravi reviewed the schedule for discussions for upcoming Planning Commission meetings, and 
said that the focus of this discussion is to review the Comprehensive Plan as a whole and 
discuss the Future Land Use Map.
Ravi said that his goal is for the final form of the Comprehensive Plan to be less than 50 pages, 
and to focus more on the goals and objectives. Ravi said that an appendix would include 
information in depth and help fulfill statutory requirements. Brian and Thomas suggested 
providing an executive summary to give a briefer overview of the City’s goals and objectives.
Ravi reviewed the draft future land use map, noting that the map was pulled from the regional 
future land use map prepared by the Chittenden County Regional Planning Commission 
(CCRPC). Trevor asked for clarification about hamlets. Ravi said that hamlets are irrelevant to 
the Winooski context, and that this applies to smaller towns with village centers that are smaller 
than the main village center. Brian asked about the boundary around the downtown core, asking 
if this denotes the area as Tier 1A. Ravi said that the City decided to have the downtown core 
under Tier 2 under his recommendation because of the existing Act 250 permit for the area, and 
the administrative burden to regulate existing Act 250 permits. Mike asked if other municipalities 
have applied for Tier 1A. Ravi said he’s aware that South Burlington has applied for Tier 1A, that 
he has had conversations with other planners in the county about Tier 1A applications, and that 
further discussion would be needed if the City wanted to apply for Tier 1A for any part of the City.
Mike asked about the orange area in Gilbrook. Ravi said that this is identified as “transition/infill”, 
and is more nebulous in terms of future land use compared to the other designations. Ravi said 
that this delineation in Gilbrook matches the current zoning map, which shows part of Gilbrook in 
the Public District and part of Gilbrook in the Industrial District. Mike said that the interest is to 
maintain flexibility in terms of land use for that portion of Gilbrook because it can be accessed 
via Hercules Drive in Colchester. Thomas asked about the future land use plan maps for 
Colchester. Ravi said he wasn’t sure, will follow up with Colchester, and will show the regional 
future land use map right now. The attendees reviewed the regional future land use map in 
Colchester. Mike discussed conversations in 2000 about the possibilities of sports facilities in 
the northern portion of Gilbrook that did not occur in the end. Bryn asked about the rationale to 
continue to reserve the northern portion of Gilbrook for future use instead of preserving the 
current usage of the area as a park. Ravi said that the designation of the northern part of 
Gilbrook is a valid conversation to have, and that in his view, developing the northern portion of 
Gilbrook would be challenging considering the location of wetlands.
Thomas and the Planning Commission discussed the feasibility of development of other parks 
in Winooski. Brian asked about the implications of designating lands in the future land use map. 
Ravi said that the zoning map need to be connected to the future land use map, and that 
depending on how the City designates lands in the future land use map could impact what areas 
could be rezoned as.
Ravi asked the attendees about the categories in the map, adding that the categories and the 
names can be modified as long as the intent matches the future land use map. Ravi suggested 
changing “Planned Growth Area” into “Residential Neighborhoods” and “Downtown Center” into 
“Downtown”. Mike suggested changing “Enterprise” into “Industrial” to match the current zoning 
terms. Thomas asked about the alignment of the areas with the parcel lines. Ravi said that for 
the most part, the boundaries between areas matches parcel lines except for floodplains, but 
that could be modified so that the designations match parcel boundaries instead.
Discussion: Review of Unified Land Use and Development Regulations – Zoning 
Mechanics and Housing Incentives
Ravi gave an overview of the presentation on the recent updates to the Unified Land Use and 
Development Regulations he gave to the Development Review Board in August 2026. Ravi 
reviewed the incentives in the current regulations for priority housing projects and inclusionary 
housing projects. Ravi explained that the incentives for priority housing projects and inclusionary 
housing projects can be used in combination with parking reductions with Transportation 
Demand Management Requirements.
Bryn asked about streamlining accessory dwelling unit allowances. Ravi said that the current 
regulations meet the statutory requirements in terms of permitting for accessory dwelling units, 
and that past conversations about accessory dwellings for multiunit dwellings were at an 
impasse and could be revisited later. Ravi said that he and Public Works are considering 
potential utility impacts with new detached accessory dwellings behind existing houses.
Brian asked about parking requirements for the residential districts. Ravi said that one can opt 
into the transportation demand management requirements in the residential districts and get a 
15% reduction in parking in the residential districts. Ravi said that past discussions on 
transportation demand management were focused on where bus lines were in the City.
Brian asked about the work involved with removing front porches from lot coverage 
requirements. Ravi said this would be relatively straightforward by defining front porches and 
including it in the exemptions in the definition of lot coverage.
City Updates
Updates from the Mayor
Thomas reviewed City Council’s discussions on revamping City boards and 
committees, and said Council was considering combining committees—such as 
combining the Housing and Planning Commissions—or reconfiguring committees. 
Thomas said that a questionnaire will be sent out to current board and committee 
members. Thomas and Mike discussed the role of the Housing Commission and 
whether staff are already covering the role and responsibilities of the Housing 
Commission. Ravi recommended that the Planning Commission not be expanded 
because any expansion would affect the reliability of regular quorum for the 
commission.
Updates from the Inclusion and Belonging Commission
Updates from City Staff
Ravi said that the Armory (50 Park Street) has been warned for a public hearing on 
September 17th, and that the surveys on the Comprehensive Plan goals and 
actions are on the City website.
Other Business
Ravi said that the Armory (50 Park Street) has been warned for a public hearing on September 
17th, and that the surveys on the Comprehensive Plan goals and actions are on the City 
website.
Adjourn
Motion by: Brian
Second: Trevor
Meeting End Time: 8:22 pm
